paths.name: @/lib/supabase/admin
paths.message: Service-role client — it ignores every RLS policy and reads SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY. Reaching it from anything that can be bundled puts that key in the browser, and this repo is public. Only src/lib/send-push.ts and the two secret-gated API routes may import it; if a client screen needs this, call an API route.

paths.name: @/lib/send-push
paths.message: Imports the service-role client transitively, so the same rule applies: server-only. Call /api/notifications/send or /api/notifications/test instead.

patterns.message: Service-role code (src/lib/supabase/admin.ts and everything importing it) is server-only. The relative spelling is restricted too so the rule cannot be stepped around by accident.

paths.name: @/lib/supabase/admin
paths.message: Service-role client. Never in a queryFn or mutationFn — it bypasses RLS, and RLS is the only thing scoping these queries to one family.

paths.name: @/lib/send-push
paths.message: Pulls in the service-role client. Server-only.

paths.name: @/lib/supabase/server
paths.message: Server client — depends on next/headers. Query functions take their client as an argument so the same module works on the web and in React Native.

paths.name: @/lib/supabase/client
paths.message: Do not reach for a particular client here. Take a DbClient argument instead; the web passes the browser client, React Native will pass its own.

patterns.message: src/lib/queries must stay free of next/*: it is the piece that ports unchanged to the React Native client.
Query functions are plain async functions over a Supabase client. Hooks and key usage belong in the components; keeping them out is what keeps this directory portable and testable without a renderer.
Server-only or platform-specific. See the named entries above.
